title: Backfill weeks 1 to 8 prices before anything else
why: It is the only item that changes what any rate on this site means. The method is proven and the bottleneck is call count, not uncertainty.
risk: The relay may not retain every historical market; where it does not, the row is dropped and the drop is published.

title: Re-express the CLV gate in points of line
why: The gate currently cannot be satisfied by any capture, because it asks for basis points while the data is in points. A gate that cannot be satisfied is not a gate.
risk: Changing a gate after seeing results invites tuning. Mitigation: the new threshold is set from the distribution of line moves, not from our own record.

title: Grade on a per-week rolling window, including the models
why: The first version of this desk rated week 9 using a standings page published after week 9. That is lookahead and it flatters any model. The window is now explicit and per-week, and it must stay that way.
risk: Early-season weeks have thin history, so week 1 and 2 rows carry almost no information. They are marked rather than hidden.

title: Publish the model's own error next to every hit rate
why: This is what stopped a 13-of-15 record being read as an edge. Without the error comparison, the site would have led with the flattering number.
risk: None identified. It makes the desk look worse, which is the intended effect.

title: Expand depth charts from 4 clubs to all 32
why: Requirement 6 is satisfied where the chart exists, and the join already demonstrates the mechanism. Doing 28 more clubs before the price backfill would trade the decisive gap for a supporting one.
risk: Leaves requirement 6 partially satisfied, which is stated on the page rather than glossed.

title: Model player props from the captured target series
why: The data has targets but no prices. A prop model without a two-way price produces a number that cannot be bet and cannot be graded against a market. It would be activity, not evidence.
risk: None: the requirement stays open and blocked, honestly labelled.

title: Add a second price provider for cross-checking
why: A second provider would let the desk test whether a movement is market-wide or book-specific. Valuable, but it multiplies the relay problem rather than solving it, so it waits behind a direct source.
risk: Two relays are still relays. The desk must not average them and call the result a market price.

title: Exercise the demotion gate on a replayed live ledger
why: The gate is defined and executable but has never fired. A trigger that has never been exercised is a configuration, not a control. Replaying a week of paper bets through it would prove it fires.
risk: A replay is not a live test. The page must say so and must not claim the gate is proven in production.
